_doc: Minor powers (Systems/Powers.cs): strong outside factions with a leader, a goal and a price, who side with the town or with one of its enemies. Standing settles toward base plus each liked signal (0-1, see Powers.Signal) times its weight, plus the favour the town's gifts bought (which fades by favourFade a day). At allyAt the town can pay price and then tithe a day for the ally boon; a town ally whose standing falls below leaveBelow, or whose tithe goes unpaid lapseDays, walks away. Allying angers its rivals by rivalHit. From courtFrom on, every courtEvery days the strongest risen enemy whose wits allow it courts one power that serves (serves 'any', the enemy's kind not in shuns): its offer is its power times its wits (cunning) times offerPerPower; if that beats the power's standing (plus allyResist when it is the town's ally) word comes through a witness and the town has noticeDays to raise standing past the offer with gifts (giftCost gold, giftFavour favour, each gift worth giftFalloff less than the last until they fade). Otherwise it joins that enemy: it arms it daily, skims the treasury, strikes with a Blows kind every strikeEvery days and adds host to the enemy's army at the walls. It goes back to neutral (standing reset to freedFavour favour) when that enemy dies, or comes back to the town early once standing reaches winBack. Each enemy takes at most perEnemy powers, and every power already marching with it adds bandwagon to its next offer. Envoys: from envoys.from, every envoys.every days the power with the most pressing case sends the town one (evil powers below tributeBelow demand tribute of gift x tribute, powers within allianceWithin of allyAt offer an alliance at price x allianceDiscount, others at pactAt or better that could serve an enemy offer a pact for gift x pactPrice: no enemy can buy them for pactDays). The town has answerDays to answer; refusing costs declined favour (spurned for a demand), and a lapsed answer is a refusal. Favours (favours): powers with asks offer to be done a favour (clear a known lair up to maxTier, see the worst enemy dead, open one more trade route); a promise has days to keep, done pays done favour and gift x gold, broken costs failed. Feuds (feuds): from feuds.from every feuds.every days the pair rested longest feuds for days; the side whose foe is the town ally holds hit against the town and, if evil with a strike, strikes every strikeEvery; the ally sends an aid envoy for gift x aid gold that wins the feud (aidFavour to it, lost from its foe; refusing costs spurned). A power with strange prices asks one instead of gold with strangeChance: name (a townsperson departs), harvest (farms yield amount less for days), voice (amount Mandate). Every power needs a library faction (ref) and a faction lineage in history.json.
_contactDoc: First contact: the town knows no power at the start. Each is met on its meetDay (its people come calling), or earlier when the town hears an enemy courting it or an ally feuding with it. A first meeting opens its contact story (contacts, also "contact-people" for the peoples, met from world.json standing meetFrom every meetEvery days; source "contact", needs ["minor"]); the "minor" effect moves its standing and favour. Unmet powers send no envoys, take no gifts and can't be allied.
warnText: {witness} brings the watch word from {name} just in time: {by} had people in the town tonight, and they are taken before they can strike.

powers.title: Factor-General
powers.goal: wants every road on the frontier to pay the Ledger a toll, and every debt collected
powers.seat: its counting-house in the Free Ports
powers.witness: a Ledger factor drinking in the tavern

ally.text: a share of the Ledger's trade paid into the treasury, and its blades on the walls

enemy.text: Ledger arms for {enemy}, and smugglers skimming the treasury

powers.title: guildmaster
powers.goal: wants contracts, gold, and no one asking where it sleeps
powers.witness: a frightened go-between who wants it known he had no part

ally.text: one of the worst enemy's captains killed every season

enemy.text: a knife in the night for one of the town's own every season

powers.contractText: Word comes by a nameless boy with a black ribbon: one of {enemyLeader}'s captains was found in the morning with a dagger that casts no shadow. {enemy} is the weaker for it.

powers.title: Lamplighter
powers.goal: wants no tyrant, cult or fiend to rule the frontier
powers.seat: nowhere, and every inn with a lantern in the window
powers.witness: a travelling singer with a lantern pin inside her collar

ally.text: warnings to the watch, so a third of enemy agents' blows are stopped

enemy.text: nothing: it never serves the town's enemies

powers.title: League Marshal
powers.goal: wants every town on the frontier walled, garrisoned and sworn to answer the beacons
powers.witness: a League herald in a ring-of-towers tabard

ally.text: League levies standing on the walls

enemy.text: nothing: it never serves the town's enemies

powers.title: Scarlet Archmagister
powers.goal: wants an enclave in every rich town, and first claim on every relic dug out of the wilds
powers.seat: the Vermilion Spire on the old Caldor road
powers.witness: an apprentice who ran from the Spire

ally.text: war-mages and wards on the walls

enemy.text: war-mages marching with {enemy}, and curses on the town's stores

powers.title: Ember Queen
powers.goal: wants a hoard worthy of her father, and every lesser wyrm gone from her sky
powers.seat: the Ember Court in the smoking peaks
powers.witness: a kobold who fled the Court with singed scales

ally.text: the Ember Queen herself over the walls when a host comes

enemy.text: the Ember Queen flying with {enemy}'s host, and fire on the roofs

powers.title: eldest of the coven
powers.goal: wants bargains struck and favours owed, and a town afraid enough to come asking
powers.seat: a stilt-house in the drowned fens
powers.witness: a hedge-witch who will not say how she knows

ally.text: a hex on the worst enemy, so its strength withers a little each day

enemy.text: rot in the town's stores and blight in its fields

strange.text: the name of one of the town's folk, freely given
strange.paid: {person} walks out toward the fens one misty morning, humming a tune nobody taught them, and is not seen again. The Grandmothers have their name.
A grey hare is seen in every field at dawn. The farmers say the soil has gone tired: the Grandmothers are taking their year of good harvests.

strange.text: the mayor's voice, a little of it
strange.paid: The mayor wakes hoarse and stays hoarse. At the council table the townsfolk lean in to hear, and some stop bothering. The Grandmothers keep what they took in a stoppered jar.

powers.title: Knight-Robber of the Rose
powers.goal: wants hoarders robbed and the takings handed out on the village greens
powers.seat: a ruined chapel in the greenwood that every forester knows and none will name
powers.witness: a charcoal-burner with a red rose pinned to his hat

ally.text: masked knights on the walls, and a share of what they take from the enemy's paymasters

enemy.text: nothing: they rob tyrants, not towns

powers.title: Matron of the Purse
powers.goal: wants three orphanages fed, and every purse in reach a little lighter for it
powers.seat: the back stair of the Harrowgate orphanage
powers.witness: a barefoot boy who knows far more than a boy should

ally.text: word from every street child in town, so a fifth of enemy agents' blows are stopped, and a cut of the take for the treasury

enemy.text: little hands in the treasury for {enemy}, and the town's purses picked

powers.title: Postmaster of the Skyhold
powers.goal: wants every road and pass carrying its letters, and every stamp paid
powers.seat: the griffon eyries of the Skyhold, above the clouds
powers.witness: a dwarven courier who lands in the square, stamps a letter and is gone

ally.text: letters flown in from every road, so warnings come in time and the stamps pay the treasury

enemy.text: {enemy}'s orders flown fast between its camps by griffon

envoys.alliance: An envoy of {name} rides in under a flag of truce. {leader}, {title}, offers {town} an alliance for {price}, less than they ask of most: {boon}. The envoy waits {answer} days for an answer.
envoys.pact: An envoy of {name} comes to the town hall with a sealed letter from {leader}. For {price}, {name} will swear a truce: it takes no enemy's gold while the truce holds. The envoy waits {answer} days for an answer.
envoys.demand: An envoy of {name} stands in the square and reads out {leader}'s demand: tribute of {price}, or {town} will learn what it costs to slight {name}. The envoy waits {answer} days.
envoys.accepted: {town} gives the envoy of {name} {price}, and {leader} keeps the bargain: {terms}.
envoys.refused: The council sends the envoy of {name} home with nothing.
envoys.lapsed: The envoy of {name} waited in vain for an answer and rode home.
envoys.pactEnds: The truce with {name} has run out. Its door is open to any enemy's gold again.
envoys.bandwagon: Word is that {backers} already march with {enemy}, which makes the offer look the safer.

ask.clear: An envoy of {name} brings a favour {leader} would have of {town}: {task}. {name} will not forget a friend who does it. The envoy waits {answer} days for an answer.
ask.slay: An envoy of {name} comes with a request from {leader}: {task}. Do it, and {name} will count {town} a friend. The envoy waits {answer} days for an answer.
ask.route: An envoy of {name} asks a favour of {town}: {task}, so that more coin moves on the roads. The envoy waits {answer} days for an answer.

task.clear: {town} gives the envoy of {name} its word: it will {task} within {days} days.
task.slay: {town} gives the envoy of {name} its word: it will {task} within {days} days.
task.route: {town} gives the envoy of {name} its word: it will {task} within {days} days.

favours.kept: {town} has done what {leader} asked: the favour is done, and {name} sends {gold} gold with its thanks.
favours.broken: {leader} hears that {town} did not do as it promised. {name} will remember the broken word.

pairs.why: a Lanternbearer singer found dead with a shadowless dagger in her back
the Ledger's tolls on the League's beacon roads
a book of names the Conclave stole out of the drowned fens
a dragon's egg the Conclave keeps under its Spire
a Lanternbearer who found out what the Ledger smuggles

feuds.begins: {witness} brings word of a feud: {name} and {foe} are at each other's throats over {why}.
feuds.callToArms: {leader} sends to {town}, ally to ally: the war with {foe} goes hard, and {price} would end it. Refuse, and {leader} will remember who stood aside.
feuds.won: With {town}'s gold behind it, {leader} drives off {foe}. {foeLeader} sues for peace, and {foe} will remember who paid for it.
feuds.ends: The feud between {name} and {foe} cools, for now.
feuds.strikes: {leader} sends agents against {town} for keeping company with {foe}.

text.courted: {witness} says envoys of {enemy} have been seen at {seat}, offering {name} gold and promises. An answer is due in {days} days.
text.refused: {witness} says {name} sent {enemy}'s envoys away empty-handed. {town} can breathe easier.
text.allied: {leader}, {title} of {name}, takes {town}'s gold and gives their word: {boon}.
text.broke: The council sends {name} word that {town} no longer needs them. {leader} takes the news coldly.
text.freed: {witness} says {name} gave up {enemy}'s cause, with no one left to pay for it.
text.wonBack: {witness} says {name} turned their back on {enemy}. {town}'s gifts outweighed the enemy's gold.
text.hexed: The Grandmothers' hex lies on {enemy}: its warriors sicken in their camps.

contacts.title: A factor of the Black Ledger

stages.text: A factor in a silver-chained coat lays a ledger on your table. {minorLeader} would like {town}'s roads on its books.

success.text: You settle on a toll that suits you both. The factor writes your name in black ink.

failure.text: The factor smiles thinly and writes down a higher number.

success.text: You catch the clause that would have bled the town dry. The factor is impressed.

failure.text: The small print beats you, and the factor knows it.

success.text: The factor bows out. The Ledger will remember a town with a spine.

failure.text: The factor laughs at you, then leaves.

ignored.text: The factor waits two days for an audience, then rides off and closes the book.

stages.text: The factor closes the ledger. "What would {town} have of the Ledger, then?"

success.text: {minorLeader} sends back warm words: {town} will be remembered kindly.

failure.text: The words come out stiff, and {minor} takes them politely and no more.

success.text: The gift goes off to {minorLeader}. It is well received.
{town} keeps its counsel, and {minor} will be back.

ignored.text: Nobody answers, and {minor}'s envoy goes home.

contacts.title: A note with a black ribbon

stages.text: A note with a black ribbon turns up on your pillow: the Silent Knife takes contracts in {town} now.

options.label: Send word you might have work

success.text: A second note comes: the Knife will hear your offer when you have one.

failure.text: No answer comes, but the watch finds a dagger driven into your door.

success.text: The watch turns out in force. The Knife notes a town that is hard to scare.

failure.text: The extra guards see nothing at all, and the town feels watched.

options.label: Burn the note and say nothing

success.text: You read the silence right: the Knife takes it as neither yes nor no.

failure.text: Your silence is taken as contempt.

ignored.text: The note goes unanswered, and the Knife marks {town} as a town that would rather not know.

stages.text: A second ribbon, red this time: the Knife asks what {town} wants of it.

success.text: {minorLeader} sends back warm words: {town} will be remembered kindly.

failure.text: The words come out stiff, and {minor} takes them politely and no more.

success.text: The gift goes off to {minorLeader}. It is well received.
{town} keeps its counsel, and {minor} will be back.

ignored.text: Nobody answers, and {minor}'s envoy goes home.

contacts.title: A singer with a lantern pin

stages.text: A travelling singer plays one song in the square and asks for you by name. She wears a lantern pin inside her collar.

success.text: She tells you which roads are watched and by whom. The Lanternbearers have a friend here.

failure.text: She sings another song and tells you nothing.

options.label: Offer her a room and a purse

success.text: She takes the room and leaves the purse. Word goes round the inns that {town} is a friend.
Your people follow her to a lantern-lit inn and learn the sign of the Lanternbearers.

failure.text: She spots them on the first corner and is gone by morning.

ignored.text: She plays her one song, waits a day, and walks on.

stages.text: The singer tunes her lute. "The Lamplighter will want to know what you'd ask of us."

stages.text: A herald in a ring-of-towers tabard rides in and reads out the Crown League's charter: every frontier town should keep a wall and answer the beacons.

success.text: The herald writes {town} into the League's roll of beacon towns.

failure.text: The herald doubts you will keep your word.

success.text: You walk the walls and talk about old sieges. The herald rides off impressed.

failure.text: He finds the gaps you hoped he wouldn't.

options.label: Tell him to mind his own towns

success.text: He bristles, but tells his marshal you are no one's vassal.

failure.text: He tells his marshal that {town} is rude and badly walled.

ignored.text: The herald reads the charter to an empty square and rides on.

stages.text: The herald rolls up the charter. "What shall I tell the Marshal {town} wants of the League?"

stages.text: An apprentice in scarlet robes asks about relics found in the wilds. Archmagister Quill would pay well for first claim on them.

success.text: You hold your own, and the apprentice writes to the Spire about you.

failure.text: You get the words wrong, and the apprentice smirks.

options.label: Promise first claim, for a price

success.text: The Conclave agrees, and sends a down payment.

failure.text: The apprentice offers far too little, and you both walk away.

success.text: The apprentice goes pale. The Conclave makes a note of it.

failure.text: The apprentice only laughs.

ignored.text: The apprentice waits a week in the inn, then goes back to the Spire with nothing.

stages.text: The apprentice bows. "The Archmagister will ask what {town} wants of the Conclave."

stages.text: An old woman at the well asks the mayor a riddle. The townsfolk cross the street to keep away from her.

success.text: She cackles and says the Grandmothers will remember your name. You wish they wouldn't.

failure.text: Wrong answer. She keeps a lock of your hair for it.

success.text: She eats, bound by the old courtesy, and blesses the well.

failure.text: She spits out the salt. The well water tastes of the fens for a week.

options.label: Have the watch run her off

success.text: She goes, but she smiles as she goes.

failure.text: She's gone before the watch arrives, and the milk sours in every house.

ignored.text: She asks her riddle three times, then walks into the mist.

stages.text: The old woman laughs like a kettle. "And what does the little town want of us, dearie?"

stages.text: A kobold with singed scales climbs the town hall steps. The Ember Queen wants to know who rules beneath her sky.

options.label: Answer with honour and a gift

success.text: The kobold takes the gold and promises the Queen will hear of {town}'s courtesy.

failure.text: The Queen thinks the gift a pittance.

options.label: Name the old wyrms you know of

success.text: The kobold hisses with glee. The Queen's rivals are the Queen's business.

failure.text: You name a wyrm she ate a century ago. The kobold is not amused.

success.text: The kobold bows low. Defiance amuses the Queen, for now.

failure.text: The kobold runs. That night a shadow passes over the roofs.

ignored.text: The kobold waits on the steps until dark, then flies home on a smoking wind.

stages.text: The kobold puffs up. "Queen asks: what does {town} want of the Ember Court?"

stages.text: Riders from {settlement} come to the gate: {people}, sent by {leader} to see who has settled so near.

success.text: The riders eat well and sing louder. They will tell {leader} the new town keeps a good table.
You trade news of the roads, and the riders warm to you.

failure.text: The talk goes nowhere. The riders leave polite and no wiser.

success.text: The riders see a town that guards its gate, and respect it, a little.

failure.text: The riders ride off muttering. {leader} will hear that the new town is rude.

ignored.text: Nobody comes to the gate. The riders wait a day, then turn for home.

stages.text: Before they ride home, the riders ask what {town} hopes for from {settlement}.

success.text: They promise to carry warm words to {leader}.

failure.text: The words come out stiff, and the riders nod politely.

success.text: You guess what they are short of, and they buy a little of it on the spot.

failure.text: You misjudge what they need, and nothing changes hands.

success.text: {town} keeps its counsel, and the riders go home.

ignored.text: Nobody answers, and the riders go home.
